summary.text: A gravida 3 woman aged 38 years was admitted with pelvic pain, diarrhea and oral lesions. For an ectopic pregnancy she had MTX at 50 mg/m^(2) when β-hCG was 2279 mIU/mL, and a second dose seven days later for elevated β-hCG and a 2-cm gestational sac in the right fallopian tube. Emergency laparoscopic salpingectomy was performed for tubal rupture with hemorrhage.

She was discharged on the first postoperative day and readmitted with bloody diarrhea, oral lesions and macular rash. She was pale with normal vital signs; hemoglobin was 6.4 gr/dL, white blood cells 2000 /µL, creatinine 1.76 mg/dL and β-hCG 91 mIu/mL. During clinical follow-up her general condition deteriorated; on the same day hemoglobin was 6.2 gr/dL and white blood cells 1600 /µL.

She was transferred to intensive care with a high serum MTX level and received calcium folinate, erythrocyte and thrombocyte replacement, intravenous hydration and nutrition, antibiotics and sodium bicarbonate. High MTX levels continued and her cytopenic state worsened; plasmapheresis was then performed and the MTX level decreased.
Her symptoms and clinical findings regressed, and after 18 days of hospitalization, including one week in intensive care, she was discharged with no symptoms.
